title: Reconciliation and component identity
description: Learn how React decides which parts of the UI to update, reuse, or throw away through reconciliation and component identity rules.

data.text: When state or props change, React does not rebuild the entire page. Instead, it runs **reconciliation**: a process that compares the new element tree with the previous one and decides the minimal set of DOM changes needed. Understanding this process explains why some updates are fast and others are unexpectedly slow.

React identifies components by their **type**. If a component at a given position changes type — for example, from `<Profile />` to `<ErrorPage />` — React tears down the old subtree and builds a new one from scratch. The old component unmounts, its effects clean up, and the new component mounts fresh.

items: Same type at the same position: React updates the existing instance
Different type at the same position: React unmounts the old tree and mounts a new one
Position matters: moving a component to a different parent changes its identity

data.text: Inside lists, React uses a child's **key** to track identity across renders. Keys tell React which items moved, which were added, and which were removed. Without stable keys, React falls back to positional matching, which can destroy and recreate components unnecessarily.

data.title: Using stable keys correctly
data.content: Stable keys let React preserve component state and DOM nodes when items reorder.

items: Using array index as a key in lists that can reorder, insert, or delete
Generating keys on the fly with `Math.random()` or `Date.now()`
Changing the key value intentionally to force a remount
Forgetting that keys must be unique among siblings, not globally

data.title: Index keys cause silent bugs
data.text: When you use array indexes as keys and the list changes order, React reuses the wrong component instances. Form inputs keep old values, animations play in reverse, and scroll position jumps. Use a stable identifier instead.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Reconciliation is the algorithm that minimizes DOM mutations
Component type determines identity at a given position
Stable keys preserve component state during list updates
Bad keys cause silent UI bugs that are hard to debug
data.takeaway: If a list feels janky or input values jump around after updates, inspect your keys first before profiling rendering performance.
